ratings_why.fun: Every buff becomes a 'who do I hang on' puzzle and the curve goes from additive sprigs to Oak and Viscum multipliers, but the fall cascades and thin Patron pool make some games feel stuck.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because the tribe can never be buffed directly: it only grows by copying hosts, including other tribes' engines, which no Battlegrounds tribe or generic auto-battler tribe does.

verdict_why: Ruin Ivy's text can still be read as redirecting rising itself, an infinite loop; one wording fix, then it is ready to settle.

points.text: Ruin Ivy should say rising itself is never redirected. As written, a Climber's copied gain is 'stats a card gives your Climbers', so it bounces to the host and copies forever.
Turns 2 to 4 hinge on finding one of five Patrons; a mono board that misses them has vanilla Climbers. A second Tier 2 Patron or a Tier 1 Climber that can stand alone would smooth the opening.
Lady Hedera grows about one name a turn and only for the fight; letting the book also give a small permanent gain at, say, five names would give the capstone a late-game arc you can see building.

In the Great House build the hub is always your biggest unit, so Honeysuckle Flatterer is free gold every turn; a condition tied to placement (host in the back row, or host with a full Hold) would keep it a choice.

standouts.why: Cousin Dodder turns the rule on the enemy: he rides their biggest unit and pays out when it dies.
The Grand Oak is a capstone the whole board is built around, and its doubling has a clear, fragile shape.
Ruin Ivy opens spells and Harvest Supper to a tribe that otherwise can't use them, at the right tier.

weakest.why: Ivy Bush is a bare Hold 2 body with nothing to decide.
Ivy Solicitor mostly moves stats and carries the one exception players must remember.
Hazel Wand's slow Health trickle does little after the first few turns.

flags.note: Does rising count as stats given to a Climber? If yes, Ruin Ivy loops forever.
Grand Oak or any host that is another tribe's scaler (an Ooze that Eats its own grown Climbers) can roughly double its gain each cycle; golden Oak with Hold 4 is about x13.
Viscum with Kissing Bough gives every Climber +1/+1 per host each turn, growing with hosts times Climbers.
